clues: This city stands on the River Vistula in the east of central Europe. A full quarter of its land is parks and green space.
Winters here are cold, cloudy, and at times snowy. Summers are warm and bright, but short, sharp storms roll in often.
King Sigismund the Third moved his court here in 1596. He made this city the capital in place of an older royal city.
War in the 1940s left the old town in ruins. Its people built it back, brick by brick, just as it had stood.
The government of Poland sits in this city. It is the seat of rule for the whole land and its biggest city.
